transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Sunday, November 8. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. Netanyahu's comeback bid: What happens if Eisenkot fails to form govt in Israel. Gadi Eisenkot has been tasked with forming a new government after the recent elections. His coalition currently lacks the required seats for a majority, presenting significant challenges. Possible support from Arab parties or ultra-Orthodox factions could aid his efforts. If unsuccessful within 42 days, Benjamin Netanyahu may receive another chance to form a government. Blast at Ghaziabad police outpost, terror link under probe. An explosion occurred at the Vasundhara police outpost, resulting in property damage but no serious injuries. A little-known outfit claimed responsibility, calling it an attack against the government. Initial investigations considered various causes, including a possible malfunction or illegal firecrackers. Security agencies are currently tracking digital leads related to the incident. Samvat 2083 outlook: Stocks, sectors and levels investors should keep an eye on. As the festive season of Diwali draws near, investors are keenly eyeing the future of Dalal Street for the forthcoming Samvat 2083. According to Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund, attention should be given to high-quality stocks while keeping a diversified portfolio. Despite global uncertainties, the domestic growth outlook in India looks promising, which is beneficial for corporate profits. Zuckerberg pledged to donate 99 percent Meta shares; here's the open letter they wrote. Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan have committed to donate a significant portion of their wealth to philanthropy. Their initiative focuses on advancing human potential and promoting equality for future generations. They aim to address challenges like disease, education, and internet access through long-term investments. The couple believes technology plays a crucial role in effecting positive change in communities. 75+ Diwali messages, wishes and quotes to spread joy and light 2026. Diwali is approaching, and many people will exchange festive greetings with family, friends, and colleagues. The article provides a variety of messages suitable for different recipients, including family, friends, and professional contacts. Short and humorous options are available for WhatsApp messages as well as heartfelt wishes for those living far away. It emphasizes conveying personal and warm sentiments to make each greeting special. From rupees 50,000 pickle startup to national award: Kerala woman's spice success. Bindulekha S faced financial struggles after her garment business collapsed due to Covid-19. She borrowed rupees 50,000 and started making pickles, quickly gaining popularity and expanding her product range. Support from organizations helped her improve food-processing techniques and marketing strategies. Bindulekha's venture, Shri Krishna Pickles, now includes several women and a roadside eatery. Fresh Houthi threat? Saudi Arabia issues potential danger alerts in 3 cities. Saudi Arabia's civil defence on Sunday issued warnings of potential danger in three eastern cities, Dammam, Dhahran and Abqaiq, amid heightened security concerns following a series of attacks claimed by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels. UK manager fired over £21,000 pothole bills wins £34,326 unfair dismissal case. A Dundee transport manager who worked for a furniture company for over 24 years was dismissed after it questioned £21,360 in pothole repair bills. A tribunal found that the company had failed to investigate the matter fairly, overlooked findings that cleared him of wrongdoing and wrongly dismissed him. It ordered the company to pay him £34,326. 'They should go to jail': Trump demands action against Democrats, orders DOJ probe. US President Donald Trump has ordered the Department of Justice (DOJ) to immediately investigate Democratic lawmakers, accusing them of threatening senior administration officials, Republican donors and political supporters with impeachment, prosecution and imprisonment. Florida landowner wins $40k over fibre cables; court limits legal fee clause. A recent ruling by the Florida Supreme Court clarified that attorney-fees clauses do not automatically apply to future property owners. The case originated with an easement agreement involving Crown Castle South LLC and RJ's International Trading LLC. Although RJ's secured damages for trespass, it sought attorney fees based on the original agreement. The court determined that the legal-fees clause lacked connection to the use or enjoyment of the land. Michael Dell is funding South Korea's most-expensive divorce ever. Michael Dell is investing $406 million in SK Group by purchasing shares from chairman Chey Tae-won. This transaction involves a 1.34 percent stake in SK Inc, aimed to fund a divorce settlement. Chey Tae-won is selling shares totaling 944 billion won to pay his ex-wife. The investment showcases Dell's connection to SK Group through their partnership in technology infrastructure.
